Warehouse transfer

Move some of one item from one warehouse to another in the same company, and check the stock at both.

Status
Verified
Module
Warehousing
Length
7 tasks, 47 steps
Updated
1 Nov 2026

Start

Summary

TaskWhat you doResultSteps
1Read the stock and the order typeYou've written down the on-hand at both warehouses, and the order type LN should give the transfer7
2Create the transfer orderThe transfer order is saved, with transaction type Transfer and one line for the item12
3Read the activities and create adviceYou've written down the activities that are yours, and the outbound line is Released or further on9
4Pick the itemsThe outbound line's Picked Quantity in Inventory Unit is filled in5
5ShipThe shipment says Confirmed, and the outbound line says Shipped6
6Receive at the destinationThe receipt says Confirmed, and the stock is in the destination warehouse5
7Verify it workedThe source is down and the destination is up by the quantity you moved3

Before you start

  • You need an item with stock in one warehouse, and a second warehouse in the same company to move it to. To find where the item has stock, follow Check an item's inventory.

Procedure

1Read the stock and the order type

Result
You've written down the on-hand at both warehouses, and the order type LN should give the transfer.
Session
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 (whwmd4300m000)

Why LN works this way. Nothing changes yet. You check a transfer at both ends, so you need the stock in both warehouses before you start. LN picks the transfer's order type from Default Order Types by Origin. That order type decides which later steps LN does by itself.

StepActionYou should see
1.1Type the item in the filter box above the grid's Item column and press EnterThe item's row, and a row for any item whose code starts with it
1.2Tick the item's own rowThe links at the top turn on
1.3Under Inventory at the top, click Warehouse InventoryWarehouse - Item Inventory (whwmd2515m000) opens with your item already in itWrite downitemsource warehousesource on-hand before
1.4In the same grid, find the row for the warehouse you're moving the items toWrite downdestination warehousedestination on-hand before
1.5Open Warehousing➔Master Data➔Order Procedures➔Default Order Types by Origin (whinh0120m000)The table of default order types opens
1.6Click the arrows on the toolbar until Order Origin reads Transfer (Manual)The rows for a transfer you enter by hand
1.7Find the row with transaction type Transfer, ship-from Warehouse and ship-to WarehouseOrder Type and Create Shipment are at the right end of the row. Between two warehouses, Create Shipment should read AlwaysWrite downexpected warehousing order typecreate shipment

2Create the transfer order

Result
The transfer order is saved, with transaction type Transfer and one line for the item.
Session
Warehousing➔Orders➔Orders (whinh2100m000)

Why LN works this way. A warehousing order you enter by hand has no sales or purchase order behind it, so Warehousing gives it its own number. LN fills in the origin, the transaction type and the order type, and you check them. For a transfer inside one company, this one order carries the whole move: first shipping out of the source, then receiving into the destination.

StepActionYou should see
2.1Open Warehousing➔Orders➔OrdersWarehousing Orders (whinh2100m000) opens
2.2Click NewWarehousing Order (whinh2100m100) opens with the origin, transaction type and order type already filled in
2.3Check the first box beside OrderIt reads Transfer (Manual)
2.4Check Transaction TypeIt reads Transfer
2.5Under Ship-From, enter the source warehouse from step 1.3 in Code
2.6Under Ship-To, enter the destination warehouse from step 1.4 in CodeBoth types read Warehouse, which a transfer needs
2.7Under Order Information, compare Order Type with the one from step 1.7Write downactual warehousing order type
2.8Click SaveWrite downtransfer order number
2.9On the Outbound Lines toolbar, click NewA new line, numbered 10
2.10Enter the item from step 1.3 in Item
2.11Enter the quantity to move in Ordered QuantityExampleOrdered Quantity 10Write downtransferred quantity
2.12Click SaveThe line says Open
Create the transfer order: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
No order number appearsThe header isn't saved, or a box is still empty. Check steps 2.3 to 2.7 again
What you type in the ship-to warehouse box is lostWith LN's menu panel open, that box can sit past the window's edge. Hide the panel with the menu button at the top left, then type it again

3Read the activities and create advice

Result
You've written down the activities that are yours, and the outbound line is Released or further on.
Session
Warehousing➔Orders➔Outbound Line Status Overview (whinh2129m000)

Why LN works this way. The order type brings a list of activities, and the order or its line can change it. The line's Activities table is the only place that says which steps LN does by itself and which are yours. Read it before you go on. If you guess, you may do a step twice or miss one.

StepActionYou should see
3.1Open Warehousing➔Orders➔Outbound Line Status OverviewOutbound Line Status Overview (whinh2129m000) opens
3.2Filter Order on the order number from step 2.8The transfer's line. If the order has other lines, the transfer's is the one whose origin reads Transfer (Manual)
3.3Tick the line and click Drill InThe line's detail opens. Order Type matches the one from step 2.7
3.4Read each row in the Activities table, above all Finished and AutomaticAutomatic Yes means LN does it. No means you do
3.5Write down the activities whose Automatic is NoYou'll do these in the next tasksWrite downmanual outbound activities
3.6Go back to the Warehousing Order tab and click ProcessLN does the automatic activities in order, and stops at the next one that's yours
3.7If Generate Outbound Advice is yours, tick the line on the Outbound Lines tab
3.8Choose Actions➔Advice➔Generate AdviceAdvised Quantity in Inventory Unit fills in. Automatic steps after it may finish too
3.9If Release Outbound Advice is yours and Released Quantity in Inventory Unit is still empty, choose Actions➔Advice➔Release AdviceReleased Quantity in Inventory Unit fills in
Read the activities and create advice: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
Advice is greyed outYou may be on the screen's own toolbar, not the Outbound Lines toolbar. See step 3.7

4Pick the items

Result
The outbound line's Picked Quantity in Inventory Unit is filled in.
Session
Warehousing➔Outbound/Inspections➔Picking List (whinh4525m100)

Why LN works this way. Picking is a step only in a warehouse that uses locations, and it's yours only if the Activities table says so. Otherwise LN fills it in for you. It works like picking for a sale, on the transfer's outbound line.

StepActionYou should see
4.1Find the Picking List row in the activities you read at step 3.4If it isn't there, or LN already finished it, write down Automatic and stop here. If its Automatic is No, carry on
4.2Open Picking List and find the run for the order from step 2.8The line for your item and source warehouse
4.3Tick the line
4.4Choose Actions➔Pick RunThe stock moves from its location to staging, and Picked Quantity in Inventory Unit fills in on Outbound Lines
4.5Read Run at the topWrite downpicking list run
Pick the items: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
No run appears on the Picking ListIf the order has already moved on, LN picked it. Write down Automatic. Otherwise go back to step 3.7 and generate the advice

5Ship

Result
The shipment says Confirmed, and the outbound line says Shipped.
Session
Warehousing➔Shipments➔Shipments (whinh4130m000)

Why LN works this way. A transfer between two warehouses always makes a shipment. Only a transfer inside one warehouse doesn't. Freezing locks what's on the shipment, and confirming takes the stock out of the source warehouse. The activities you read at step 3.4 say whether you do this or LN does.

StepActionYou should see
5.1On the Warehousing Order for the order from step 2.8, open the Shipment Lines tabThe shipment line for your item. The shipment number is the first part of Shipment Line, before the line number:Write downshipment number
5.2Find the Freeze/Confirm Shipments/Loads row in the activities you read at step 3.4If LN already finished it, the shipment line is Confirmed, so stop here. If its Automatic is No, carry on
5.3Open Shipments and filter Shipment on the shipment number from step 5.1Your shipment's row
5.4Tick the row and click Drill InShipment opens. Status = Open
5.5If Freeze Mandatory is ticked, click FREEZE on the toolbarStatus = Frozen
5.6Click CONFIRM on the toolbarStatus = Confirmed. The stock leaves the source warehouse
Ship: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
No shipment line showsBetween two warehouses there should always be one. Check the activities from step 3.4, and whether the line is picked yet
CONFIRM is greyed outThe shipment isn't frozen yet. Do step 5.5 first

6Receive at the destination

Result
The receipt says Confirmed, and the stock is in the destination warehouse.
Session
Warehousing➔Orders➔Orders (whinh2100m000)

Why LN works this way. The same order now does its second half, receiving into the destination. A transfer is received on the same receipt screen a purchase uses. Confirming the receipt is what puts the stock into the destination warehouse.

StepActionYou should see
6.1On the Warehousing Order for the order from step 2.8, open the Inbound Lines tabThe inbound line, Open. The destination warehouse is under Ship-To at the top
6.2Tick the inbound line
6.3On the Inbound Lines toolbar, choose Actions➔Receive…Warehouse Receipt (whinh3512m000) opens for the destination warehouse, with the line's full quantity receivedWrite downreceipt number
6.4Tick the receipt line
6.5Choose Actions➔ConfirmThe receipt says Confirmed
Receive at the destination: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The inbound line isn't there yetThe shipment isn't confirmed. Go back to step 5.2

7Verify it worked

Result
The source is down and the destination is up by the quantity you moved.
Session
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 (whwmd4300m000)

Why LN works this way. Nothing changes. A confirmed receipt is only a status. The proof is the stock: down at the source and up at the destination by the same quantity. One can be right while the other isn't, so you read both.

StepActionYou should see
7.1Type the item in the filter box above the grid's Item column and press EnterThe item's row
7.2Tick the item's own row and click Warehouse InventoryWarehouse - Item Inventory (whwmd2515m000) opens, one row for each warehouse
7.3Read Inventory on Hand in the source's row and the destination's rowAgainst steps 1.3 and 1.4, the source is down by the quantity from step 2.11, and the destination is up by the sameWrite downsource on-hand afterdestination on-hand after
Verify it worked: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The destination's on-hand didn't go upThe receipt may not be confirmed. Go back to step 6.5
The two changes aren't both the quantity you movedSomething else may have moved the item in one of the warehouses. Look for other orders on the item before you trust the result

Variations

Variations
CaseWhat changes
Between two companies — the warehouses belong to different logistic companiesLN makes two warehousing orders instead of one. The shipping company's order ships the items, and the receiving company's order receives them. That changes the tasks, so it would be a guide of its own
Planned by LN — the transfer comes from order planningTransfer Order Planning (cppat1210m000), under Planning➔Plan Transfer➔Transfer Order Planning, makes transfer orders from planning, so nobody enters one by hand. It's a different guide
Serial or lot numbers — the item is tracked by serial or lotThe order header's Reclassification tab matters for these items. This guide doesn't cover them

The stock is in the destination warehouseShip from stock, to ship it from thereConfirm there is stock
